subject: Credential propagation fallback activated — short-notice hotfix
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Lee <jamie.lee@acme.com>, account_manager@acme.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 01:12:00 +0000
Subject: Credential propagation fallback activated — short-notice hotfix

Hi Jamie / Acme team,

Quick heads up: we pushed an unscheduled hotfix at 01:05 UTC to address intermittent 401s some Private deployment customers started seeing overnight. Root cause: a race in the credential-propagation microservice that causes new tokens to occasionally not be written to the downstream cache under specific burst patterns. That manifested as auth failures for a subset of streaming requests.

What we did immediately:
- Activated a fallback routing rule that directs auth traffic to the previous stable propagation service instance (safe read path). This reduces latency slightly but prevents the 401 spike.
- Deployed a 8-line hotfix to the propagation worker (hotfix_patch.diff attached).
- Enabled short-term request tracing for any auth 401s (repro_log_excerpt.txt attached).

Customer impact:
- If you saw elevated 401s between ~00:45–01:05 UTC, those requests should now be routed correctly.
- No stored user tokens were deleted or exposed; the issue is write visibility only.

Action we recommend for customers:
- Please validate normal API calls from your integration; if you have automated health checks, expect one quick spike while the routing settles (under 5 minutes).
- Optional: if you rotate keys frequently and want to be proactive, hold on rotation for 30 minutes after confirming behavioral normalcy.

We know short notice is disruptive — apologies for that. We prioritized preventing auth failures while we prepare a more complete fix and tests. I’ll loop in the runbook and the follow-up timeline in a second message.

Attachments: hotfix_patch.diff (code stub), runbook_credprop_v2.pdf (short-runbook), redirect_policy.yaml, repro_log_excerpt.txt

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 04:35:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Credential propagation fallback activated — short-notice hotfix

Hi Jamie — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Retries/processing: The affected requests that returned 401 during the window were not processed server-side (auth failed before request handling). If your client retried on 401 it should succeed now; if you keep a record of request IDs, we can run a targeted replay if you prefer.

2) Audit/log evidence: yes — we recorded the redirect and fallback events in our auth-audit stream. See ticket INC-20261109-42 (link above) for the sliced logs; the attached repro_log_excerpt.txt includes an anonymized example with timestamps. Full logs are available on request and we will share an export under your existing support agreement.

3) Risk and data: there was no data exposure or token leakage. This was a propagation visibility issue only.

4) Permanent fix timeline: engineering will merge the full fix + tests by EOD UTC 2026-11-10 and schedule a small zero-downtime rollout during a low-traffic window (TBD with you). We will also add the e2e burst test Ben mentioned.

Immediate ask from Acme: if you can confirm whether you retried the affected requests, we will prioritize targeted replay and attach the actual request IDs to the support ticket.

I’ll follow up with a short postmortem draft later today. Thanks again for the quick flag — we want to make sure this is fully remediated and transparent.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
